stats.fact: Apeireth is a 17-crate Rust workspace (16 crates in the core kernel + assembly) enforcing acyclic single-direction dependency across 4 layers: foundation, engine, capabilities, adapters.
Written in Pure Safe Rust with #![forbid(unsafe_code)] / #![deny(unsafe_code)] — zero unsafe blocks, zero data races, zero unhandled exceptions.
Hybrid memory search (BM25 + dense cosine + RRF fusion over 10,000 nodes) measured at 1.82 ms P99, well under the 10 ms target.
Cognitive quota preemption dispatch measured at 8.40 µs P99 (target < 50 µs); causal world model CoW fork + 100-file snapshot diff at 0.035 ms; SAGA compensating rollback at 0.012 ms.
Microkernel cold start (17-crate workspace bootstrap to ready) measured at 4.20 ms; runtime idle footprint ~18.2 MB RAM (target < 35 MB).
The workspace runs 3,119 unit and integration tests across the crates, with 0 clippy warnings enforced via cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings.

9 cognitive organs are fully implemented: E4 Curiosity, F1 Emotion Memory, F4 Hypothesis, F6 Value Cases, W1 World Model, W2 Causal World Model, W3 Causal Edge Mining, E7 Emergence, and Memory Merger.
W1 World Model is LLM-heavy: it runs counterfactual reasoning chains via a TextualSimulator + TimelineLlm, calibrated at the endpoint with oracle Brier scores to prevent confabulation.

W2 Causal World Model runs LLM-driven MCTS counterfactual 'if...then...' paths over the memory_graph s/p/o causal network; W3 Edge Mining is deterministic (no LLM) and mines causal edges from the owner's memory timeline.

F1 Emotion Memory records the owner's mood as a 2D valence/arousal timeline (half-life 4h decay), with mood trend and recall-by-mood — explicitly framed as the owner's emotion as data, not simulated AI emotion.

E7 Emergence uses rhythm learning (histogram of when the owner is likely active), relationship pressure growing with silence duration x warmth (Borbely sleep-pressure-style homeostasis), and an 8-gate constitution (quiet hours, daily limit, LLM budget, min depth).

Ember HUD provides ambient physiological presence: a 4.0s breathing curve I(t)=I0+A·sin^3(2πt/4) with Planckian blackbody color temperature (3200K idle amber, 5500K deep thinking, 2200K circadian dreaming, 4200K flow focus).

Triple-Onion zero-trust security: L0 immutable human authority (500ms fail-closed), E/S/A/M/O principle onion with Ed25519 epigenetic invariance, L1-L5 permission escalation, Colang/ASI-01 DSL guardrails, plus physical OS sandbox (Windows JobObject / Linux cgroups + Git worktree rollback).
Portable USB flash-drive agent with relative ./data/ isolation and Noise_XX end-to-end encrypted P2P mesh roaming (BLE/LAN) for zero-cloud memory sync.
Repo is young: created 2026-09-04, 27 stars, 1 fork, 0 open issues, dual-licensed Apache-2.0 OR MIT.

angles: The 'Companion Organ' framing: Apeireth treats the AI companion not as a chat box but as a set of cognitive organs (emotion memory, care potential, emergence rhythm) that compute how to make the owner's day better — with an explicit '0 fake pass' honesty boundary that it does NOT simulate AI emotion.

World Model as the differentiator: W1/W2/W3 split LLM-heavy counterfactual reasoning (W1, W2) from deterministic causal edge mining (W3) over the owner's personal memory timeline — a 'world model trained on one person's life' rather than a generic world model.

Pure Safe Rust as a safety argument: #![forbid(unsafe_code)] + physical OS sandbox + SAGA rollback positions memory safety and fail-closed governance as the foundation for trustworthy AGI, contrasting with Python/LangChain/AutoGPT stacks.
The honesty engineering ('0 装 PASS') philosophy: no todo!(), no unimplemented!(), no dummy mocks, no hollow stubs — and the W1/W2 organs genuinely call the LLM rather than pretending to.
Benchmark-driven credibility: sub-millisecond P99 latencies and ~18MB idle footprint make a concrete, verifiable case that a Rust cognitive microkernel can be both fast and memory-safe.
The emotional narrative: the README opens with a story about remembering a deceased parent's small preferences — positioning 'remembering what you forgot' as the core companion value proposition.
